title: vidstabtransform leaves a shallow copy of the source frame in the library's state
live_proof: the fix's removed lines are present from n8.0 through n8.1.2 and absent from 9.0.x
object: the source frame's plane storage, named by libvidstab's td->src with no reference taken
lifetime_ender: the filter returns the source frame, and the pool reissues its storage to the next frame
fidelity: allocator literal, consumer and library both reduced: libvidstab is not linked, and its state is modelled as the one retained pointer the upstream message describes
distinguishing: the corpus's only write probe, and the only case where the retained pointer lives inside third-party state rather than FFmpeg's own
note: the real filter needs --enable-libvidstab; the fixture does not, because the retained pointer is the defect

native-fix-differential.oracle: the buggy arm writes through the parked pointer into the new owner's storage; the fixed arm carries nothing across frames
native-fix-differential.note: this pair differs by the upstream fix, not by protection

sublet.oracle: fault at the labelled WRITE probe, a different published address from the read cases

poisoncap-protected.oracle: SIGPROT after the setup marker FF2_PROBE case=38 ready
poisoncap-protected.note: CheriBSD reports a process status, not a fault PC, so the marker is what separates this from an arbitrary crash: it is printed only once reuse at the same address has been checked

native-detect.requires: the port's payload arena is one allocation, so ASan's silence here would measure the fixture rather than FFmpeg

status: native pair, both domain arms and both PoisonCap arms run 2026-09-20; all passed. The PoisonCap run carried the five platform controls (live, poisoned read, poisoned write, sweep/reuse, retained old alias) alongside, so the protection is shown active independently of these cases
